title: Build agent creates a kanban grouped by a field it just added without disclosing that every existing record will be invisible on the board — extend the honest-disclosure contract (the rollup/backfill precedent) to the view face
body:
Provenance: split from objectstack-ai/cloud#1818 (filed by the maintainer from the two-plane rig, pins 8c822893/7a5da141, scenario battle R7) by the repo:cloud execution seat (objectstack#6026, session `session_01EzWYDkwr6WEwDGhMH1Jzuq`, R30). This is the **builder-side half**; the view-side half (kanban fallback lane) is objectstack-ai/objectstack#13692 (`repo:objectui`). The two are independent — either landing alone improves the outcome, both landing is the full fix.

## Measured behavior

In battle R7 the build agent added a 「客户等级」(A/B/C) select field to an existing customer table AND created a kanban grouped by it, in one request. Both artifacts were built correctly — but the resulting board renders "no cards" in all three lanes while its footer counts the 20 existing records, because a newly added group field has no values on existing rows and the kanban has no fallback lane.

## The ask

When the build agent creates a view grouped by a field that (a) it created in the same request, or (b) measurably has no values on existing records, it should proactively disclose: existing records will not appear on this board until the field is filled (and offer the obvious follow-ups — backfill, or a fallback lane once the view supports one). The maintainer's source card names the precedent explicitly (untranslated):

> 对比同一战役 R10 的教训(rollup 无 backfill 必须诚实披露),这里是同一根因的**视图面**

i.e. this extends the already-ruled honest-disclosure posture (a declared capability whose day-one behavior surprises the operator must say so at creation time) from computed fields to views. Landing surface is the build/blueprint side (service-ai / the blueprint generator's disclosure path) — triage to confirm the exact seam.

Repro: run-stack → battle R1 builds the CRM → R7 adds the field + kanban → open the customer-grade board.
